key_insight: Boundary-layer detachment and breakdown of Prandtl scaling can coexist with numerical convergence toward a smooth Euler flow as Reynolds number increases.
engineering_relevance: The findings help distinguish local near-wall complexity from global inviscid-limit accuracy when assessing high-Reynolds-number flow models.
method: Run highly resolved direct numerical simulations in a two-dimensional periodic channel with no-slip walls.
Construct Reynolds-dependent initial conditions with Prandtl-thickness boundary layers converging to a stationary Euler flow.
Track detachment, velocity-error energy, dissipation, and detached-vortex structure.
evidence_signal: Over the simulated interval, both the squared energy norm of the velocity difference and time-averaged energy dissipation scale approximately as Re^(-1/2), supporting convergence despite detachment.
watch_item: The evidence is numerical and limited to the simulated two-dimensional configuration and time interval; it does not establish general or long-time convergence.
paper_title: Boundary-layer detachment and infinite-Reynolds limit of two-dimensional wall-bounded flows
